name: STIHL MS 400 C-M
blurb: 3/8″ chain, .050″ gauge: 66, 72, 84 and 91 drive links on 18″, 20″, 25″ and 28″ bars, per STIHL's 2025 chart.
intro: The MS 400 C-M is in the same 2025 chain-chart block as the MS 362, MS 362 R, MS 362 C-M and MS 362 R C-M. The MS 362 has its own page. The .050″ rows that read cleanly for this block are 33 RS3: 66 links on 18″, 72 on 20″, 84 on three different 25″ bars, and 91 on 28″. Several of the longer bars are marked with an asterisk (yellow-labeled; no reduced-kickback bar listed at that length).

bars.note: STIHL's chart lists chain 33 RS3 66 with recommended bar 3003 008 8917. STIHL's 2025 file table lists a 5.2 mm (13/64″) file for 3/8″ chain. Oregon's 2020 filing chart gives 7/32″ for standard 3/8″ chain (types 72, 73, 75).

STIHL's chart lists chain 33 RS3 72 with recommended bar 3003 008 8921. STIHL's 2025 file table lists a 5.2 mm (13/64″) file for 3/8″ chain. Oregon's 2020 filing chart gives 7/32″ for standard 3/8″ chain (types 72, 73, 75).

STIHL's chart lists chain 33 RS3 84 with recommended bar 3003 000 4030. STIHL's 2025 file table lists a 5.2 mm (13/64″) file for 3/8″ chain. Oregon's 2020 filing chart gives 7/32″ for standard 3/8″ chain (types 72, 73, 75). The chart marks this bar with an asterisk: a reduced-kickback bar is not listed at this length.

sources_note: STIHL 2025 Full Line catalog chain chart (catalog pp. 166–167), read 5 Nov 2026. Only .050″ rows whose marketing number matches the drive-link column are listed. File size: STIHL 2025 file table (13/64″ for 3/8″) and Oregon's 2020 filing chart (7/32″ for standard 3/8″ chain).
notice: STIHL's 2025 chart also prints a .063″ section in this model block. In that section the chain marketing numbers do not line up with the drive-link column (a count is printed next to a loop whose marketing number is a different count, or a .050″ loop is printed on a .063″ row). Those combinations are not listed. If your bar is stamped .063″, use the stamp.
